relationship: Repayment to an enemy: conditional oath and narrative
rationale: The psalm puts repaying those who repay the speaker evils under its conditional self-curse. The Saul narrative explicitly distinguishes David's repayment with good things from Saul's evil repayment. The comparison concerns reciprocal response without adding an object to the psalm's first repaid.

relationship: Preserved life and praise at God's dwelling
rationale: The psalm asks for mercy from the Lord who raises from death's gates so the speaker may praise at daughter Zion's gates. Hezekiah contrasts living praise with Hades and promises continual blessing before God's house. Both connect life preserved from death with worship at the holy place.
